name: OPA604 / OPA2604 (Burr-Brown FET-input, low-distortion audio op-amp)
tagline: Burr-Brown's early-90s FET-input audio op-amp with on-chip distortion rejection and ±24 V rails; the warm, "tube-like" (胆味) classic of CD-player, sound-card and phone Hi-Fi.
technology: FET-input voltage-feedback op-amp. The block diagram shows 'Distortion Rejection Circuitry' and an 'Output Stage', both marked 'Patents Granted: #5053718, 5019789'. The datasheet cites new circuit techniques and special laser trimming of dynamic circuit performance for low harmonic distortion, plus a laser-trimmed offset. A copper leadframe improves heat dissipation. Supply is ±4.5 V to ±24 V (±25 V absolute maximum) per the datasheets, but a 2016 report says late OPA2604 production had to be held to ±20 V (see silicon_changes). It is unity-gain stable and drives 600 Ω. 'Difet' is a community label (Soomal 2016 groups OPA2604 with 'DiFET-structure' parts); the OPA2604 datasheet does not use the word.

lineage.period: c. 1991-2000 (OPA2604 datasheet ©1991; OPA2604E PSpice macromodel 'revised 3/21/92'; OPA604 datasheet ©1992)
lineage.notes: Burr-Brown was headquartered in Tucson, AZ; the fab location is not stated in the datasheets. Datasheets were PDS-1069x (OPA2604) and PDS-1161x (OPA604). No second sources are known.

The datasheets were renumbered SBOS006 (OPA2604, September 2000) and SBOS019 (OPA604, SBOS019A revised September 2003). SBOS006 kept the Burr-Brown PDS-1069E body until SBOS006A (Dec 2015) moved it to the TI template. Both BB-logo and TI-logo markings appear in teardown photos (Soomal). The OPA2604 dual went EOL c. 2016 (diyAudio 'OPA2604 is dead', 24 Aug 2016, reports a lifetime-buy period); TI E2E threads (2019) confirm it is no longer available. The OPA604 single is ACTIVE on ti.com. A TI E2E FAQ names OPA1656 as the 'next-generation OPA2134 and OPA2604 replacement'.

reputation.summary: One of the defining 'Burr-Brown sound' op-amps. English forums call it warm, laid back and easy to listen to. Japanese PC-audio and headphone bloggers call it 'the legendary op-amp' (伝説のオペアンプ, e.g. southenst.com), with gloss (艶), spaciousness, fat bouncy bass and soft, smooth highs; nabe ranks it B+ (not re-verified). Soomal (2010) calls it an op-amp with a strong '胆味' (valve flavour), and Soomal (2013) says its fame among enthusiasts is 'not much lower than NE5532'. Soomal teardowns confirm it in the vivo Xplay and Xplay 3S (OPA2604AU), Smartisan T1, Sony PHA-3 (two as LPF after ES9018S), Shanling H3A (I/V and LPF), SoundAware M1 and A280III, TempoTec Serenade USB and Teclast T51. Its ±24 V rating made it one of the few audio op-amps usable on high rails. In a 2016 review Soomal rated warm DiFET-type parts (including OPA2604) above OPA1612-type parts for audio on average. Newer Japanese listening tests (new_western_elec 2025, not re-verified) rank it below MUSES8820/8920 and NL8802/NL8902.
sonic_descriptors: laid back, easy to listen to
typical_uses: CD player and DAC output / I-V stages (PCM DAC I/V converter is a datasheet application)
DAC low-pass filter stages (Sony PHA-3, Shanling H3A, SoundAware A280III/M1)
PC sound-card and USB DAC op-amp rolling
Smartphone Hi-Fi audio paths (vivo Xplay/Xplay 3S, Smartisan T1)
Maverick D2 DAC stock part; Fosi rolling kit (not re-verified)
Professional audio line stages on high (±18 to ±24 V) rails
caveats: Fast (20 MHz GBW): a translated English headphone-amp op-amp survey (translated by 杜毅 for DiyEden, reposted by Soomal 2005) reports that an OPA2604AP oscillated above about 18 V in one Hansen-type amp but ran at 34 VDC in other amps. The author called it much harder to use than OPA132/134 and heard it as nearly identical to them.

Needs adequate rails: the 0.0003% THD is specified at ±15 V. Soomal measured the Teclast T51 running it at about ±9.5 V and called the claim unachievable. Soomal said the Smartisan T1's OPA2604 showed high distortion, and that phones need a boost converter for it (T2 switched to OPA1612).
Soomal (2010, T51 context): driving low-impedance headphones directly makes it sound thin and harsh, with more bass distortion.
Some Japanese reviewers (Mineden) find the midrange thin (not re-verified).
Colored 'warm' voicing: 2025 Japanese tests prefer newer parts for resolution (not re-verified). Meizu's 2014 marketing showed a CMRR chart favouring OPA1612 over OPA2604.
OPA2604 (all packages) is EOL since c. 2016, so most market stock is fake (see counterfeit notes).

High-rail use is the weak point: TI E2E says OPA2604 performance could not be guaranteed near its ±24 V limit because of heat/package dissipation, and a 2016 diyAudio report says late parts had to be held to ±20 V (offset drift and rising Iq at ±24 V). Keep late-lot or unknown-origin OPA2604s at or below ±20 V.

revision_history.changes: OPA604 Burr-Brown datasheet (PDS-1161C / May 1995 confirmed by web search summary). Revisions A and B and their change contents were not found.
OPA604 TI re-issue under SBOS numbering (date confirmed by web search; ti.com lists Rev. A as current). Change contents not captured. Fits TI's 2003 addenda on ex-Burr-Brown sheets.

OPA2604 Burr-Brown datasheet (confirmed via transcription and web-indexed copies). Includes the 'Distortion Rejection Circuitry' block diagram (patents 5053718, 5019789), a copper-leadframe power-dissipation note and θJA 90 °C/W. Revisions A-D not found.

revision_history.date: September 2000 (TI original date per the SBOS006A revision history); distributed copies carry a package addendum dated 3-Oct-2003
revision_history.changes: Same Burr-Brown PDS-1069E body stamped 'SBOS006', with a TI Package Option Addendum (OPA2604AP, AU and AU/2K5 all ACTIVE). No content changes observed.

Template conversion: added ESD Ratings, Feature Description, Device Functional Modes, Application and Implementation, Power Supply Recommendations, Layout, Device and Documentation Support, and Mechanical/Packaging/Orderable sections. Thermal table became per-package (SOIC RθJA 107.9 °C/W, PDIP 46.7 °C/W); recommended operating conditions added (±4.5 to ±24 V, -40 to 100 °C). Electrical characteristics unchanged. Still states ±24 V although a ±20 V constraint was reported in 2016. Appears to be the last revision before EOL.

silicon_changes.when: c. 2015-2016 (TI 'Non-conforming' form quoted in the diyAudio thread 'OPA2604 is dead', 24 Aug 2016). Datasheet SBOS006A (Dec 2015) still specifies ±4.5 to ±24 V.
silicon_changes.identification: No marking, datasheet or PCN change. The derating was communicated through a TI non-conformance form, not a datasheet revision. Affected date codes are unknown; late TI-logo lots are the suspect population. Per diyAudio, the OPA604 single does not have the thermal problem.
silicon_changes.summary: Unannounced supply derating under the same part number. TI told customers that the OPA2604 no longer supports ±24 V and must be constrained to ±20 V: at ±24 V, parts showed large long-term offset drift and increased supply current, thought to be thermal (the dual runs hot). A TI E2E answer gives the same reason for the later discontinuation: performance could not be guaranteed near the published ±24 V limit because of heat and package dissipation. Whether a die or process change caused it is not known.

spec_deltas.after: ±20 V (non-conformance constraint; never printed in a datasheet)

spec_deltas.before: Fully specified (PSRR spec covers ±5 to ±24 V)
spec_deltas.after: Reported long-term large offset drift and increased Iq

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Only high-rail designs (±20 to ±24 V pro-audio line stages, some DIY amps) are at risk: offset drift and extra heat. Typical ±15 V op-amp rolling is unaffected; distortion and noise at compliant supplies are unaffected.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - designs that rely on the OPA2604's ±24 V rating may drift or run hot; drop-in only at ±20 V or below; ±15 V use unaffected
silicon_changes.verification: Merged two reports. WebSearch confirmed that diyAudio quotes a TI 'Non-conforming' form (OPA2604 must be constrained to ±20 V, offset drift and extra current at ±24 V) and that a TI E2E answer cites heat near ±24 V as the EOL reason; no PCN, datasheet revision or die/process evidence was found.

silicon_changes.when: EOL stated by TI engineers on E2E by about 2019-2020 (threads 766644 and 953479). In Aug 2016 diyAudio reported it as officially Active but effectively unobtainable (lead time over 6 months, commercial quantities only).
silicon_changes.identification: Lifecycle status only. DigiKey lists OPA2604AU/2K5 as obsolete, and OPA2604AP is widely listed as obsolete. The E2E asker noted that TI published no PCN or PDN. OPA604 (single) remains Active on ti.com.
silicon_changes.summary: The OPA2604 dual was discontinued (TI E2E: 'OPA2604 has EOL status'). TI suggested two OPA604 singles, or OPA2134 or OPA1656, as alternatives; diyAudio users cite OPA1688 as an official replacement. It was the only dual high-voltage JFET-input audio op-amp on the market, so no dual drop-in exists for ±20 V+ rails. No die or fab PCN beyond the supply derating was found.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None to the silicon. Parts sold now are old stock or possibly remarked fakes. Suggested replacements are different dies and sound or measure differently.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - the dual is no longer made; the OPA604 needs a two-package adapter, and OPA2134/OPA1656 are not rated for ±20 V+ rails
silicon_changes.verification: Split out of the sweep entry. WebSearch confirmed a TI E2E engineer stating OPA2604 EOL, with OPA604 still Active and OPA2134/OPA1656 as alternatives. No PDN number was found, so the exact EOL date is uncertain.

counterfeit_notes: Fakes are extremely common for the OPA2604, and all remaining stock is post-EOL. A survey by the 'fakecomponents' account (19 Sep 2019) found 70 of 75 OPA2604s bought individually on Yahoo Auctions were fake (93%); the new_western_elec blog (Oct 2019) reported it and advised against buying there. The nabe blog has a 'fake-looking TI op-amp' post, and a Yahoo Chiebukuro Q&A discusses fake OPA2604s ordered from abroad. Reported fakes include remarked TL072-class dies, markings that wipe off with ethanol, and sanded or re-coated tops without moulded rounded edges on thinner bodies (not re-verified). Kokoro-navi (2011) reportedly documented fake OPA2134PA/OPA2604AP, and a fake was reported inside an Aune mini USB DAC (both not re-verified). TI E2E has an 'original or fake OPA2134/OPA2604' thread. Soomal (2010) compared a genuine part from a TI channel, a market fake and the chip pulled from a Teclast T51: the fake was obviously fake; the T51 chip differed from the genuine one only in marking clarity. Soomal stress-tested the T51 chip at ±23 V; it burned out, which proved nothing (and late genuine parts are reportedly not rated for ±24 V anyway). Tests: marking durability under solvent, package edge and mould finish, and parameters against the datasheet. A genuine OPA2604 draws about 10.5 mA total (max 12 mA at ±15 V) with 20 MHz GBW and 25 V/µs, versus about 3 MHz and 13 V/µs for a TL072 remark. Genuine SOIC parts are marked 'OPA 2604AU' (TI addendum). BB-logo and TI-logo lots are both genuine; no die change is documented, but late lots reportedly need rails held to ±20 V. Safest route: buy the still-active OPA604AP/AU from authorised distributors and use two on a dual adapter.
alternatives: OPA1656 (TI CMOS; named in a TI E2E FAQ as the 'next-generation OPA2134 and OPA2604 replacement'; ±2.25 V to ±18 V per SBOS901C, so not a ±24 V drop-in)
OPA1642 (TI JFET-input; suggested on TI E2E as a lower-noise, low-distortion OPA2604 alternative when 20 MHz is not needed; ±18 V max)
OPA2156 (TI CMOS; suggested on TI E2E when more bandwidth is needed; check supply limit before high-rail use)
OPA1688 (TI; reportedly suggested as an OPA2604 replacement, source not pinned down; check its supply limit)
OPA604AP/AU singles on a dual DIP-8 adapter (single-channel sibling, ACTIVE on ti.com)
OPA2134 (sibling Burr-Brown FET audio op-amp, still in PDIP but lower bandwidth; ±18 V max)
MUSES8920 (Japanese community successor; 'keeps OPA2604 softness with wider stage')

refuted_claims: Hazard hint 'TI discontinued the OPA2604AP around 2019': the diyAudio thread 'OPA2604 is dead' (24 Aug 2016) already reports a lifetime-buy period. The 2019 TI E2E threads only confirm that the part was gone by then.

Hazard hint / part status 'only the DIP (OPA2604AP) was discontinued because TI could not guarantee ±24 V in that package': the whole OPA2604 family is reported discontinued (E2E: 'no longer available from TI or their distributors'). TI's stated reason (heat and package dissipation near ±24 V) is not specific to DIP. OPA2604AU and AU/2K5 statuses changed to obsolete.

Counterfeit note 'new_western_elec found 70 of 75 OPA2604s were fake': the survey was done by the 'fakecomponents' account (19 Sep 2019). The new_western_elec blog (Oct 2019) reported it but did not run it.
corrections: Added a silicon_changes entry: the same OPA2604 part number was reportedly derated from ±24 V to ±20 V without a datasheet change, with long-term offset drift and higher Iq at ±24 V (diyAudio 2016). This matches the TI E2E EOL reason. Confidence is medium.
Lineage and part statuses: the OPA2604 family was EOL around 2016. OPA604AP and AU are ACTIVE on ti.com. Added the OPA604AU/2K5 orderable.
Added the TI E2E threads 766644 ('OPA2604 EOL?') and 953479 ('Status of the OPA2604AU/2K5, PCN available?'). The thread URL 793405 already in the draft is also confirmed.

OPA604 datasheet dates confirmed: SBOS019A is January 1992, revised September 2003, and ti.com lists Rev. A as current. PDS-1161C is dated May 1995. Added the hifituning24.de copy titled 'Rev. A'.
The radiolocman entry now uses the confirmed OPA604AP URL (di=82264). The di=306221 URL is still unconfirmed.

New confirmed mirrors: part-elec.com OPA2604AP, Octopart OPA2604AU/2K5 (8443596) and AU/2K5E4 (8442517), alldatasheet TI OPA604AP (170749) and OPA604AU (170751). Caveat about the EOL rationale rewritten: it is not specific to DIP. Users should keep late or unknown-origin OPA2604s at or below ±20 V.
claims_confirmed: The OPA2604 is discontinued. According to TI E2E, its performance could not be guaranteed near the ±24 V limit because of heat output and package dissipation. OPA1642 is suggested if 20 MHz is not needed and OPA2156 if more bandwidth is needed. https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/766644/opa2604-eol
The OPA2604 is no longer available from TI or its distributors, and TI does not mention the EOL anywhere. https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/793405/opa2604-eol

diyAudio 'OPA2604 is dead' (24 Aug 2016): a document says the OPA2604 no longer supports ±24 V and must be held to ±20 V, with long-term offset drift and higher Iq at ±24 V. A lifetime-buy period was in effect. https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/opa2604-is-dead.295854/
A TI E2E thread asks for the status and PCN of the OPA2604AU/2K5. https://e2e.ti.com/support/amplifiers-group/amplifiers/f/amplifiers-forum/953479/status-of-the-opa2604au-2k5-pcn-available

A TI E2E FAQ presents OPA1656 as the 'next generation OPA2134 and OPA2604 replacement'. https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/911603/faq-opa1656-next-generation-opa2134-and-opa2604-replacement
The OPA604 is ACTIVE on ti.com, with the datasheet at Rev. A and OPA604AP/AU orderable. https://www.ti.com/product/OPA604

The OPA604 datasheet is SBOS019A, dated January 1992 and revised September 2003. It carries PDS-1161C, printed May 1995, and covers 8-pin mini-DIP and SO-8 packages at -25 to +85 °C. https://www.hifituning24.de/downloads/opa604.pdf
The TI gpn link resolves to the OPA604 datasheet titled 'FET-Input, Low Distortion Operational Amplifier datasheet'. https://www.ti.com/lit/gpn/OPA604

The survey of 75 OPA2604s from Yahoo Auctions that found 70 fakes (over 93%) was by fakecomponents on 19 Sep 2019 and was reported by new_western_elec. https://nw-electric.way-nifty.com/blog/2019/10/post-19bc00.html
The Japanese label '伝説のオペアンプ BB(Burr-Brown)OPA2604' is confirmed. http://www.southenst.com/cgi-bin/blog/html/art/00174.html
Copies of the PDS-1069E / Oct 1997 / SBOS006 edition are hosted at hirokun.jp, media.digikey and Octopart (per search summary). https://hirokun.jp/OPA2604.pdf
DigiKey hosts a TI-template OPA2604 PDF titled 'OPA2604 Dual FET-Input, Low-Distortion Operational ...'. https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/842/OPA2604.pdf
The audiokarma 'OPA2604AP (obsolete)' and GroupDIY 'OPA2604 Substitutions' threads exist. https://audiokarma.org/forums/threads/op-amp-upgrades-opa2604ap-obsolete.935775/

revision_chain_notes:
NOTE: the task text swaps the Burr-Brown numbers. The chain file and this round's search summaries both show PDS-1069 = OPA2604 (dual; PDS-1069E, October 1997) and PDS-1161 = OPA604 (single; PDS-1161C). This round found only mirror copies; none of them show a revision letter.

(1) Burr-Brown PDS-1069 (OPA2604, ©1991), oldest to newest:
- A to D: missing (original c. 1991 issue).
- E: October 1997, confirmed.
Still missing: A–D, with dates. Candidate holders are rtellason.com/chipdata/opa2604.pdf, the datasheetarchive OPA2604 index and datasheet4u 475618; none show a letter.

(2) Burr-Brown PDS-1161 (OPA604, ©1992; the TI header gives the original date as January 1992), oldest to newest:
- Original/A: January 1992, missing.
- B: missing.
- C: ©1992, printed May 1995, confirmed again by a search summary this round.
Still missing: original/A/B, and whether a PDS-1161D (c. 1996–2000) exists. Candidate holders are alldatasheet 56786/56787, datasheetspdf/datasheet4u 475772 and the datasheetarchive OPA604 index; none show a letter.

(3) TI SBOS006 (OPA2604), oldest to newest:
- SBOS006 (unlettered): September 2000, Burr-Brown PDS-1069E body; copies carry a 3-Oct-2003 package addendum.
- SBOS006A: revised December 2015, TI template. A search summary confirmed the 'September 2000 – Revised December 2015' header this round.
The chain is complete; the part went EOL c. 2016, and a diyAudio thread names OPA1688 as a replacement.

(4) TI SBOS019 (OPA604), oldest to newest:
- SBOS019 (unlettered): TI re-issue, c. 2000; date and copy not found.
- SBOS019A: January 1992 – revised September 2003, confirmed again this round; still current on ti.com.
Still missing: an identified copy of the unlettered SBOS019.

No new revision dates or change summaries turned up, so revision_history additions are empty.

The archive_seed_urls are not from search results. They follow TI's legacy URL patterns (focus.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/<part>.pdf, focus.ti.com/lit/ds/<litno>/<litno>.pdf, www-s.ti.com/sc/ds/<part>.pdf) and must be checked in the Wayback Machine before use. They are the best way to recover the unlettered SBOS019 and older PDS letters. Burr-Brown's own legacy URLs were not found, so none were invented.
